_note: Registered on 2026-10-10 before the v7 live runs. Every proposal size was re-checked against published evidence with the same yardstick for both candidates, and every proposal against the plan text registered at the TSE. Results are published whatever they are.

rules.plan_text_only: Only proposals written in each candidate's TSE plan are modeled. Removed: Lula P08 (taxing high incomes is already law, Lei 15.270/2025; the plan mentions it in the past tense) and Flavio P14 (inflation-only health/education floors and pension/BPC floor: not in the plan, only in press reports; the candidate publicly denied cutting pensions). Added proposals found in the plans but missing before: Lula P15-P18, Flavio P17-P20.
rules.baseline_is_current_law: Programs in the 2026 budget and laws already in force belong to all three scenarios; only the increment proposed by a candidate counts. Already law: CBS/IBS tax reform, high-income minimum tax, Redata data-center regime (Law 15.504/2026), environmental licensing law (Law 15.190/2025), minimum-wage valorisation rule.
rules.credit_is_not_spending: Development-bank and FGTS credit is not primary spending; only the Treasury subsidy counts.
rules.fiscal_rule_cap: A candidate who keeps the arcabouço fiscal (Lula P01) cannot add net primary spending above about 0.1% of GDP a year; the excess is cut from discretionary spending (engine lever 'spending_cap'). Same credibility weight (business_climate 0.15) for keeping the arcabouço (Lula) and for the new surplus rule (Flavio).
rules.gdp_for_conversions: R$ 13.7 trillion in 2026 (PLOA 2027), so 0.1% of GDP is about R$ 13.7 billion.

P01.why: IMF WP 2025/195 and Itau on fiscal rules and spreads; LC 200/2023 caps spending growth at 70% of revenue growth; IFI: discretionary room near its floor.

P02.why: 0.5 equals the CNI worst case; Ipea finds no clear GDP loss; Gonzaga, Menezes-Filho & Camargo (2003) found no job loss in 1988. The PEC passed the Chamber in May 2026 and awaits the Senate.

P03.why: No evidence that ministry structure lowers homicides; conditional on the PEC.

P04.why: Body cameras cut police killings 57% in Sao Paulo; intelligence-led Pacto pela Vida; no causal evidence for asset seizure alone.

P05.why: About 90% of Nova Industria Brasil is BNDES/Finep credit; Lazzarini et al. (2015) find low additionality.

P06.why: Bolsa Familia (R$ 157 bi) and the minimum-wage rule are already in the 2026/2027 budget; the plan only commits to continuity and expansion without a figure.

P07.why: The tax reform is law for all scenarios; the plan only promises to consolidate it.

P09.why: Enforcement cut deforestation 73% in 2007-11 (AEJ Applied); further cuts are harder from today's lower base; plan target is net-zero by 2030.

P10.why: LC 221/2025 already exempts R$ 5 bi a year of strategic defense projects.

P11.why: MCMV budget subsidy about R$ 13 bi in 2026; most funding is FGTS credit.

P12.why: Pe-de-Meia (R$ 11.5 bi) already in the 2026 budget.

P14.why: Mais Medicos had no aggregate infant-mortality effect (only where it was above 25 per 1,000); Farmacia Popular is only maintained.

P15.why: Piped water and sewage reduce infant mortality (NBER w14365; FGV); investment need R$ 45-50 bi a year, mostly operators.

P17.why: Escolas Conectadas: R$ 8.8 bi plan, 99k schools already connected.

P18.why: Tax-credit swap already capped at R$ 2 bi a year by MP.

P01.why: Plan gives no amount; the campaign cites R$ 190 bi, but Executive discretionary spending is only R$ 184-227 bi and near its floor; asset sales are one-off financing. Credibility weight equal to Lula P01.

P02.why: Merging ministries saves little; -0.25 would double count with P01.

P03.why: 1 pp of CBS costs about 0.35-0.4% of GDP; fuel and energy cuts 0.1-0.3%; the plan has no food tax cut (cesta basica already zero-rated).

P04.why: Megginson & Netter (2001): firm efficiency gains; cross-country evidence finds privatization neutral for growth; Eletrobras and Sabesp already sold; plan says 'case by case'.

P05.why: R$ 225 bi a year is below today's infrastructure pace (R$ 280 bi in 2025, 84% private) and matches the existing concession pipeline; business_climate double counted the investment.

P07.why: El Salvador evidence transfers poorly (gang-pact critiques); Brazil already has 5 federal max-security prisons; mass incarceration strengthened PCC/CV.

P08.why: Minors are a small share of killers; age-18 deterrence about zero in the US (Lee & McCrary); gangs recruit younger.

P09.why: Severity deters little; certainty matters more (Chalfin & McCrary 2017).

P15.why: DETER satellite monitoring existed in 2019-21 while deforestation rose; reductions come from fines and embargoes, not detection.

P16.why: Licensing law already in force since Feb 2026; only further relaxation is incremental.

P17.why: Ipea TD 2357: 2012+ payroll tax relief had no employment effect; small fiscal cost inferred.

P20.why: Savings from benefit reviews; the associative-discount fraud took money from pensioners, not the budget.

not_modeled: Flavio's gradual CDE energy-subsidy cut: paid through tariffs, so no primary-balance effect, and about -0.1 pp on the price level by 2030 (negligible).
no_cost_preview: Replaying the v6 agent decisions with these values: 3 x 3 with the old market and central-bank reactions, Lula 4 x 1 with equal reactions; primary deficits 0.46% (Lula) and 0.37% (Flavio) with equal reactions.
runs: Main and informed versions re-run live on DeepSeek into out/scale-v7 and out/informed-v7 with the Chamber elected on 2026-10-04 (left 24.2%, Centrao 50.1%, right 25.7%).
